title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-13
content:
Date: 2026-03-13
Owner: Samir Patel
Focus: triage kv-cache leak + investigate small latency regression after last rollout + kernel sync issue

OVERVIEW / CONTEXT
- Follow-up from yesterday: rollouts/2026-03-12 introduced prefix-KV caching changes + batching improvements (PR #1142). Small fraction of requests (~0.8%) started seeing OOMs on ded08 nodes after sustained high-concurrency traffic. Also observed 2-4ms p95 latency regression on short chat requests (seq_len ~64).
- Oncall reported in #oncall and I posted initial repro steps. Working with Lina and Ethan.

BLOCKER: intermittent mem growth in kv-cache (suspected leak)
- Symptoms: resident memory steadily increases on some worker pods under heavy prefix-cache hit rate (>70%) + continuous batching. After ~2 hours, process hits soft OOM and restarts.
- Repro steps (quick):
  1) run unit load harness with prefix-cache enabled (cfg: prefix_cache=true, batch_target=64, max_seq=2048)
  2) use synthetic client that sends many distinct prefixes but repeated mid-tail tokens to exercise cache insert/evict paths
  3) monitor heap + GPU memory (nvidia-smi) and process RSS
- Hypothesis: eviction path for prefix-cache doesn't release KV cache slice references when batch coalescing happens -> lingering references in python layer (or C++ binding) preventing free. Potential race with async eviction timer.
- Quick checks done:
  - Confirmed Python refcount for CachedPrefix objects increases during sustained load (sampler attached).
  - Heap profiler snapshot attached to PR #1142 shows increasing tuples and dicts around kv_cache keys.
- Immediate next actions:
  - Add instrumentation to eviction path to log refcounts and timestamps (Samir) - TODO for today (2h).
  - Reproduce in CI harness with leaked object logging enabled (Ethan) - target by EOD.
  - If confirmed, fast rollback to previous prefix-cache variant (rollback patch drafted in PR #1148) to restore stability for Dedicated clusters. Lina to coordinate rollback window w/ infra.

PERF INVESTIGATION: p95 regressed ~2-4ms for short requests
- Observed on hosted-api and some dedicated instances after batcher change; hypothesis: batching policy now waits slightly longer to form target batches for tiny requests, adding queuing latency. Alternative: kernel selection path now chooses flash-attn2 variant which has slightly higher setup overhead for tiny seq_len.
- Data to gather:
  - Microbench: measure per-request latency vs batch size for seq_len 16/32/64 on all kernel variants (flash-attn, flash-attn2, cuDNN fallback). (Samir/Ethan)
  - Instrument batcher to emit per-request queue_time histograms (already added to staging; need to ramp).
- Action items:
  - Add quick AB test to revert batching hold-time for small requests (config flag). If p95 improves, we'll tune adaptive hold-time rather than rollback. (Lina)
  - Run microbench and post results to thread + link to PRs. (Samir)

KERNEL / CUDA NOTE (observed potential bug)
- Symptoms: occasional corruption traces when using concurrent CUDA streams for KV cache serialization + attention kernel. Suspect missing stream synchronize before memcpy on host pinned buffers.
- Location: serving-runtime/src/runtime/kv_cache/evictor.cu and serving-runtime/src/runtime/attention/kernel_wrapper.cu (see PR #1139 comment).
- Hypothesis: evictor launches async copy on streamA and then immediately queues an op on streamB that expects the host buffer content; missing cudaStreamWaitEvent or cudaMemcpyAsync ordering.
- Quick test: insert cudaStreamSynchronize(streamA) after copy and run kernel stress - reduces repro frequency. Need proper fix: use events to order streams or move to single stream for dependent ops.
- Action: file small patch to add event sync and open issue on repo (Samir). Add unit test that runs high concurrency eviction + attention kernel to reproduce if ordering missing.

MEETING NOTES
- 10:30 sync with Lina: cover rollback criteria (error rate >0.5% or OOMs >3 in 1h). Agreed: rollback if we cannot stabilize within 90m and customer impact measured. Lina will coordinate infra window.
- 14:00 quick with SRE: suggest adding node-level oom alert for process RSS > 85% to catch earlier. SRE will add transient alert.

TODOS (short)
- [ ] add eviction refcount logs + safe telemetry (Samir)
- [ ] run leak repro in CI harness and attach heap profiles (Ethan)
- [ ] prepare rollback patch and schedule window with Lina (Lina)
- [ ] microbench kernel variants for seq_len 16/32/64 (Samir)
- [ ] add batcher queue_time histograms to staging and enable for 1% sample (Ethan)
- [ ] add cuda event ordering in evictor and test (Samir)
- [ ] update incident doc if rollback occurs (Lina)

NOTES / LINKS
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1142 (prefix-cache change), PR #1148 (rollback draft), PR #1139 (cuda stream discussion)
- Jira: ENG-3421 (prefix-cache memory leak tracking)
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime, #oncall (incident comments)

ESTIMATES / TIMING
- Instrumentation + quick logs: 2-3h
- Repro in CI + heap profile: 3-4h (EOD target)
- Microbench + AB revert test: 4-6h (tomorrow morning)

RANDOM NOTES / TODOs for later
- revisit adaptive batch hold-time algorithm; consider queue_time-aware hold time that uses recent p95 at seq_len bucket
- evaluate quantized KV cache footprint improvement (whiteboard idea)

End of scratchpad.
